parts.official_mark_scheme_text: State $\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}=\sin\theta$ or $\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}=-\sin\theta+\dfrac12\sin2\theta$. B1. Use $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}\div\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}$. M1. Obtain the correct derivative in any form, for example $\dfrac{-\sin\theta+\frac12\sin2\theta}{\sin\theta}$. A1. Use the double-angle identity correctly to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $\theta$. M1; $\sin2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$. Obtain the given answer with no errors seen, $-2\sin^2(\frac12\theta)$. A1 AG. Guidance: correct cancellation of all $\sin\theta$ terms and $\cos\theta=1-2\sin^2(\frac12\theta)$ must be seen. SC: incorrect signs consistent throughout score at most B0 M1 A0 M1 A1. Total 5.
